title: Financial Conditions For The AI Capex Boom
gist: Gavekal teaser (Denyer, Tan): the AI capex boom's pain is financial, not fundamental — semis (SOX -33% since Oct 5) and data-center names fell on rising yields, sticky inflation, a hawkish Fed and post-midterm politics, while compute demand still outpaces supply; even rising GPU spot prices partly reflect tightening financial conditions forcing weaker buyers onto the spot market.

insights.claim: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 33% between October 5 and late November 2026, with CoreWeave, Oracle and Alphabet also performing poorly, as financial and political conditions for the AI capex boom worsened.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Quantifies the drawdown in AI-infrastructure equities; frames the question of whether gloom is over- or under-priced.
insights.quote: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down -33% since October 5
insights.locator: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down

insights.claim: Gavekal attributes the AI-infrastructure selloff to rising bond yields, persistent inflation, a hawkish Federal Reserve and a tougher political backdrop after the US midterm elections, compounded by the Jensen Huang affair — not to weak demand or an oversupply of compute.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The driver is cost of capital: AI-infra equities should trade on rates/Fed expectations more than on demand data.
insights.quote: The problem is neither a lack of demand nor an oversupply of compute.
insights.locator: The first thing to do is identify the source

insights.claim: AI compute demand is still outpacing supply, as evidenced by rising GPU rental prices.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Fundamental demand remains intact — a bullish counterpoint to the selloff, if financing conditions ease.

themes.theme: GPU spot prices as a financial-stress signal

insights.claim: Rising GPU spot rental prices may be less bullish than they look because they partly reflect tighter financing: data center operators now demand bigger upfront payments for long-term compute contracts, pushing financially weaker customers onto the spot market and bidding up spot prices.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Read GPU spot-price strength as a partial credit-stress indicator; watch which compute buyers are being squeezed out of term contracts.
insights.quote: rising GPU spot prices may not be as bullish as they seem
insights.locator: On a recent Odd Lots episode

insights.claim: As capital has become costlier and scarcer, AI data center operators have begun requiring larger upfront payments from customers to secure compute under long-term contracts.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Tighter contract terms shift financing risk to customers — weaker AI startups/neoclouds' customers are most exposed.
insights.locator: As capital has become costlier and harder
